Unholy Death Knight Rotation in 

Unholy Death Knight primarily operates based on resources and current procs. This generally means that what we do at any given moment will be based on both of these factors, which makes a typical rotation out of the question, and instead operates on a priority list. 

 

 

 
 Keep Abilities on Cooldown: Unholy is a very burst-focused specialization, which relies incredibly heavily on using its cooldowns as often as possible to maximize its damage. This makes cooldown setup and execution its highest priority. 

 

 

 
 Spend your Sudden Doom procs ASAP: Sudden Doom has many interactions with Unholy talents, while also being the strongest non-cooldown button we can press in any scenario. This makes spending this proc with Death Coil or Epidemic as quickly as possible one of the best things you can do. 

 

 

 
 Keep an eye on your Ghouls: Lesser Ghouls are the bread and butter of Unholy Death Knights in Midnight. So, making sure that you always have stacks of Lesser Ghoul from Festering Strike to allow Scourge Strike to summon them is vital. 
 

Unholy Death Knight Starter Guide

 Best Unholy Death Knight Rotation

Unholy Death Knights' rotational priorities are more often than not, focused on resource management. Between Runes, Runic Power, and our Lesser Ghoul stacks, Unholy has a plethora of resources to manage, and doing so well will drastically improve your DPS.

For all forms of content, Unholy follows a priority list of what spells to cast. Below, we break down the main priority lists for Unholy Death Knights: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

 Best Unholy Death Knight Single Target Rotation

Unholy in Single Target plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources based on an order of power. This means with each GCD we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value.

Priority outside of Forbidden Knowledge

 
Cast Dark Transformation on cooldown.

Cast Putrefy if Dark Transformation is active.

Cast Death Coil if you have a Sudden Doom proc.

Cast Festering Strike if you have no Lesser Ghoul stacks.

Cast Scourge Strike if you have Lesser Ghoul stacks.

Cast Death Coil .
 

Priority during Forbidden Knowledge

 
Cast Putrefy on cooldown.

Cast Necrotic Coil .

Cast Festering Strike if you have no Lesser Ghoul stacks.

 Best Unholy Death Knight AoE Rotation

Unholy in AoE plays around a priority list, juggling both ability cooldowns and resources based on an order of power. This means with each GCD we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value.

Priority Outside of Forbidden Knowledge

 
Cast Dark Transformation on cooldown.

Cast Putrefy if Dark Transformation is active.

Cast Death and Decay if you expect your targets to stay inside of it.

Cast Epidemic .

Cast Festering Strike if you have no Lesser Ghoul stacks.

Cast Scourge Strike if you have Lesser Ghoul stacks.
 

Priority During Forbidden Knowledge

Cast Graveyard .

Cast Festering Strike if you have no Lesser Ghoul stacks.

Cast Scourge Strike if you have Lesser Ghoul stacks.

 Best Unholy Death Knight Opener Priority

Unholy's Opener is fairly notorious for being a "nuclear launch sequence" to get going. This hasn't changed much in Midnight, though the sequences tend to be more simple than before.

Sequence

Use On-Use Trinket.

Use Combat Potion.

Cast Necrotic Coil .

Cast Necrotic Coil .

Cast Putrefy .
 

Pre-Combat Check

Before entering combat, it is important for Unholy Death Knights to do the following. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

Rider of the Apocalypse
San'layn
 Festering Scythe 
 Army of the Dead 
 Blightburst 
 Soul Reaper 
 Reaping 
 Blightfall 

 Unholy Death Knight Major Cooldowns

Unholy has a few major cooldowns with mechanics that may make you want to use them at specific times. Below, there's a section to go over each of these, explaining when and why you should use them when you do.

 Army of the Dead‎ 

 Army of the Dead is our biggest cooldown and serves as a trigger for many other talents. The most prominent among those would be Raise Abomination , Summon Gargoyle , and Apocalypse Now , where this ability will summon additional pets to fight for us.

With the sheer quantity of pets being summoned by this ability, if you have talented Commander of the Dead , it's vital to ensure that Army of the Dead and Dark Transformation stay in sync, so you are using both at the same time. Generally, this will mean ensuring you hit Dark Transformation as soon as possible after it comes off cooldown once between every Army of the Dead cast.

 Dark Transformation‎ 

Similar to Army of the Dead, Dark Transformation also triggers several other talents. The most important among these are Commander of the Dead , Outnumber , and Ride or Die! . 

With Commander of the Dead, it is particularly important to keep your cooldowns synchronized. With Dark Transformation being an off-global cooldown ability, you can safely macro this into Army of the Dead and only have to worry about a single use between each Army window. 

In addition to this, if you talent Outnumber, it becomes incredibly important to try to time your Dark Transformation with add spawns, as the Lesser Ghoul Sweeping Claws attacks are incredibly potent, and will constitute a major portion of our AoE damage potential. 

 Putrefy‎ 

 Putrefy is a fairly unique ability in how it should be used. With other talents allowing you to trigger Putrefy, some of which even use the charges you have for you. This is usually a short-duration cooldown, averaging about 15 seconds between uses, making it fairly rotational. 

The major talents to consider for when to use Putrefy are Soul Reaper (in addition to Reaping ). 

Now, there is a pair of talents that can throw a wrench into this logic with Soul Reaper and Reaping . Due to Soul Reaper consuming 2 of your current Putrefy charges, it can be worth not pressing Putrefy if Soul Reaper will be available to use in the next 15 seconds or so. While your target is below 35% health, this will mean you never manually press Putrefy. 

Outside of this, if you talent Reaping, you should try to bank a charge for Dark Transformation windows to save you the global and rune you would have spent on Putrefy otherwise.
